text.arabic_uthmani: فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَن يَجْعَلُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ ۚ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُم بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

words.gloss_range: sequential-resumptive particle opening the enacted consequence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the brothers' prior speech into enacted time. It resumes the story and moves it forward at once, so the new scene feels like the immediate consequence of their request rather than a neutral continuation. In {{ar:فَلَمَّا}} ({{tr:fa-lammā}}), the clipped onset also releases into the doubled timing word and helps launch a suspended temporal frame whose expected resolution will be overtaken by divine speech.

topics.headline: immediate scene consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah turns prior dialogue into immediate narrated consequence while opening a delayed time-frame for divine intervention.
topics.reason: The particle is aligned as a conjunction prefix before the temporal frame, and attachment evidence puts the following human actions under that frame.

words.gloss_range: temporal conjunction setting the brothers completed actions as the trigger frame
words.root_gloss_range: grammaticalized temporal use from a root range of gathering/contact; local use is a fixed narrative timing operator, not the negative homograph

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) sets the time-frame over the brothers completed going and resolving. The local grammar selects the temporal conjunction, not the negative homograph, so the point is a when-frame rather than denial. Its fixed adverbial form gathers human action and divine response into contact, the doubled mim audibly slows the hinge, and the expected answer to the time-clause is delayed until {{ar:وَأَوْحَيْنَا}} ({{tr:wa-awḥaynā}}) arrives.

topics.headline: temporal trigger with grammaticalized contact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers completed actions become a timed trigger where human action and divine response are brought into contact.
topics.reason: QAC marks an adverb of time governing perfect-tense clauses; root-image and rarity claims are retained only as background pressure because the local form is grammaticalized.

words.gloss_range: completed plural departure with a governed taking-with phrase
words.root_gloss_range: departure, going away, and disappearance; local construction with the attached preposition narrows it to taking Yusuf away under their control

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:ذَهَبُوا}} ({{tr:dhahabū}}) is not bare travel once {{ar:بِهِ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) follows it. The perfect plural verb reports the removal as already enacted, and the attached phrase makes Yusuf the one taken along under the brothers control. The wording shifts the earlier with-us request of 12:12 into custody by means of him, and the same movement root later becomes part of their alibi in 12:17 and later commanded departures in 12:87 and 12:93.

topics.headline: completed custody-removal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers do not merely go; the construction changes their movement into custody-removal of Yusuf.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the following prepositional pronoun as complement of the verb, supporting the custody-removal reading.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus 3ms suffix marking Yusuf as attached object of the departure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:بِهِ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) binds Yusuf to the departure verb as a suffix rather than naming him independently. The preposition keeps accompaniment, instrumentality, and control together: he is with them, but also the carried target through whom the plot proceeds. This first Yusuf reference in the ayah is grammatically minimized, then the same 3MS referent moves from vulnerable object here toward recipient in {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}).

topics.headline: Yusuf bound to the departure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Yusuf reduced to a bound suffix in the brothers movement, then later rerouted as recipient of divine address.
topics.reason: The phrase is the prepositional complement of the departure verb and the suffix is the first Yusuf reference in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle linking the two completed human clauses
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the brothers going with their resolved plan, making the motion and decision one human action block. It can carry simple coordination with a circumstantial feel, because their resolve accompanies the movement rather than waiting as a separate later scene, and the short particle lets the second human verb attach without a strong pause. That joined block prepares the later {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) before divine revelation to enter as a different agency.

topics.headline: paired human action block
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that movement and resolve are paired as a completed human block before divine agency interrupts it.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the second perfect verb as coordinated with the first perfect verb.

words.gloss_range: Form IV perfect of collective resolve taking a content clause
words.root_gloss_range: gathering and collecting, locally narrowed by Form IV and complement syntax to firm collective resolve rather than mere physical gathering

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:أَجْمَعُوا}} ({{tr:ajmaʿū}}) turns the gathering root into resolved unanimity. The following {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) clause supplies the content of the resolve, so the brothers agreement is not vague: it is directed toward placing Yusuf in the well hidden recess, at the point where their plan feels crystallized before reversal. The word also turns their earlier protective cohesion into conspiratorial cohesion, later retold inside the unseen-news frame of 12:102 and set against later regathering pressure in 12:83.

topics.headline: collective resolve made explicit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers are unified in a specified conspiracy, not merely gathered in one place.
topics.reason: QAC marks Form IV perfect and attachment evidence makes the following clause the content complement; physical gathering is narrowed to firm resolve.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle nominalizing the intended placement clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff
nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) bridges resolved intention into specified execution. It nominalizes the placement clause as the content governed by {{ar:أَجْمَعُوا}} ({{tr:ajmaʿū}}), while also carrying purpose pressure because the clause names what the decision aims to do. Its short form releases directly into {{ar:يَجْعَلُوهُ}} ({{tr:yajʿalūhu}}), so the transition from decision to planned action is abrupt.

topics.headline: resolve-to-execution bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compact grammatical bridge that turns resolve into the named placement they intend to execute.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the subordinated clause as complement to the resolve verb.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive placement verb with Yusuf as object and a locative destination
words.root_gloss_range: making, placing, appointing, and causing; local grammar selects purposeful concrete placement, with wider appointment/status-change echoes kept as secondary

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:يَجْعَلُوهُ}} ({{tr:yajʿalūhu}}) makes the plan a deliberate placement, not a random throwing-away. The 3MS suffix keeps Yusuf as the direct object, while {{ar:فِي غَيَابَتِ الْجُبِّ}} ({{tr:fī ghayābati al-jubb}}) supplies the place into which they intend to put him. The broader root can mark divine making and appointment elsewhere, as in 2:30, 17:2, and 19:30, but here that range is narrowed to human placement that will later be answered by God-given status in the surah (12:21).

topics.headline: purposeful placement into concealment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices purposeful placement into concealment, with later divine making or appointment kept as a contrast rather than the local sense.
topics.reason: The local locative complement selects concrete placing; wider appointment/status-change branches are retained only as contrastive echoes.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition governing the concealed-depth construct

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) makes the plan spatial: Yusuf is to be placed inside the hidden recess, not merely near it. The preposition governs {{ar:غَيَابَتِ}} ({{tr:ghayābati}}), creating double containment with the recess inside the well, while still letting figurative immersion in concealment be felt. Its placement after the verb delays the endpoint until the hidden destination is named, and its sound links smoothly into the following location phrase.

topics.headline: inside the concealed depth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices layered containment: Yusuf is routed inside the recess, and that recess belongs inside the well.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the noun as the prepositional complement of the placement verb.

words.gloss_range: construct noun for the well hidden recess or depth
words.root_gloss_range: absence, hiddenness, and unseen knowledge; local noun selects a physical recess, while unseen-news pressure remains active through the ayah revelation and disclosure arc

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:غَيَابَتِ}} ({{tr:ghayābati}}) names the hidden recess of the well as the intended place. Its construct form binds hiddenness to {{ar:الْجُبِّ}} ({{tr:al-jubb}}), so the scene is not generic absence but a particular concealed depth; the exact phrase proposed in 12:10 is now enacted in 12:15. Variant rows widen the image through singular, plural, shaddah, sukun, and vowel possibilities, while the local form still selects the recess. That physical hiddenness is immediately countered by revelation, by the sound texture of the well phrase, and later by unseen-news language in the same surah (12:102).

topics.headline: hidden recess answered by revelation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a physical hidden recess whose concealment is answered by revelation, variant depth, and later unseen-news disclosure (12:102).
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make this a construct noun governed by the preposition; variant and unseen-knowledge rows are retained as narrowed image and arc pressure.

words.gloss_range: definite concrete well/pit completing the hidden-recess construct
words.root_gloss_range: cutting off and pit/well imagery; local noun selects the definite well, with severance and closed-depth pressure as image support
words.prose: {{ar:الْجُبِّ}} ({{tr:al-jubb}}) completes the construct and makes the hidden recess belong to a definite well already known from the plan in 12:10. The noun is rare in the Quran, appearing only in this surah, and has the force of a raw pit or cut-off place rather than an ordinary water-source scene. Its short, doubled closure gives the pit a closed sound, so the place meant to sever Yusuf from view becomes the exact anchor where proposal becomes deed.

topics.headline: definite rare severance-pit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the definite rare well is both the repeated plan-anchor and a severance-pit image.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the genitive second term of the idafa; root and sound claims are narrowed to image support for the concrete well noun.

words.gloss_range: conjunction introducing the divine response after the human plot block

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) before {{ar:أَوْحَيْنَا}} ({{tr:awḥaynā}}) shifts the scene from the brothers action block into divine action. It can read as coordination, resumption, and circumstance, but its payoff is that revelation enters before the human plot has the last word, opening a new acoustic and agency strand. The particle also resolves the suspended temporal opening by moving from human claim and narrated deed into first-person divine voice.

topics.headline: divine countermove boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary where coordinated human plotting is interrupted and answered by first-person divine action.
topics.reason: Attachment clauses place the divine verb after the temporal human-action frame as the narrated response.

words.gloss_range: Form IV first-person plural perfect of divine communication/revelation
words.root_gloss_range: quick, hidden, directed communication; local Form IV selects revelation/communication from God to Yusuf
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْحَيْنَا}} ({{tr:awḥaynā}}) reports completed divine communication in the first-person plural. The root quick and hidden communication image fits the well scene: while the brothers hide Yusuf from sight, a concealed divine channel reaches him and performs assurance rather than report only. This first divine communication to Yusuf outweighs the preceding human verbs, joins crisis-communication patterns such as 10:87 and 28:7, and anticipates the story later framing as unseen news revealed to the Prophet (12:102).

topics.headline: hidden divine communication
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices hidden divine communication reaching Yusuf inside the concealment scene and functioning as assurance, not report only.
topics.reason: QAC marks Form IV first-person plural, and attachment evidence links it to the recipient phrase and quoted content.

words.gloss_range: directional preposition plus 3ms suffix marking Yusuf as revelation recipient

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff
nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ilayhi}}) routes the revelation toward Yusuf as its destination rather than as a burden merely assigned to him. The same 3MS referent who was bound as object in {{ar:بِهِ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) and {{ar:يَجْعَلُوهُ}} ({{tr:yajʿalūhu}}) is now the recipient of divine address, so the preposition plus suffix reverses the relational axis. A Yaqub alternative is noted in the rows, but the local pronoun chain and the revealed promise make Yusuf the primary referent.

topics.headline: object becomes recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Yusuf reversal from object of removal to destination of revelation, with the Yaqub alternative kept as apparatus only.
topics.reason: The pronoun chain and quote content support Yusuf as primary; the alternative does not control the local parse.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lām opening the promised informing clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) attaches oath-like certainty to the future informing verb. Together with the heavy nun later in {{ar:تُنَبِّئَنَّهُمْ}} ({{tr:tunabbiʾannahum}}), it creates a la...anna frame that makes the revealed content a firm divine promise rather than a possibility. Its tight opening sound and certainty answer the brothers confident speech with a stronger assurance.

topics.headline: emphatic promise opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the coming disclosure is doubly secured by the emphatic lam and the heavy nun on the verb.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as emphatic, and the following verb carries matching heavy emphasis.

words.gloss_range: Form II emphatic imperfect promising future disclosure to the brothers
words.root_gloss_range: news, significant informing, and prophetic announcement; local Form II selects decisive informing, with elevation/prophetic associations kept as secondary pressure
words.prose: {{ar:تُنَبِّئَنَّهُمْ}} ({{tr:tunabbiʾannahum}}) promises that Yusuf will decisively inform them. The second-person masculine form points to Yusuf as the canonical speaker, while variant rows show third-person and first-person plural routes for disclosure agency without displacing the local surface. The Form II news-root makes the future confrontation more than casual telling: the hidden affair will become significant news delivered to the very brothers who failed to perceive it, with prophetic/elevation pressure reversing pit-depth in the background and unseen-news fulfillment reaching toward 12:102.

topics.headline: emphatic future disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hidden deed is already secured for decisive future disclosure to the brothers themselves.
topics.reason: The local surface is 2MS with 3MP object and heavy emphasis; variants, prophetic associations, and elevation pressure are retained as narrowed apparatus or background.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the topic about which the brothers will be informed

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) turns the following affair into the topic of disclosure. Instead of a bare second object, the prepositional phrase makes the promised informing confrontational: Yusuf will inform them about, and in a sense with, their own matter. The proclitic binds the news verb to {{ar:أَمْرِهِمْ هَذَا}} ({{tr:amrihim hādhā}}) as a named case, so the disclosure has a precise target.

topics.headline: topic of disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the future disclosure has a confrontational topic, not a bare or unspecified second object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following noun phrase the prepositional complement of the informing verb.

words.gloss_range: possessed singular affair/matter naming the brothers deed as their own case
words.root_gloss_range: command, affair, matter, and authority; local noun selects their affair while divine-command pressure remains a contrastive background

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby pronoun cited to explain the payoff
nearby demonstrative cited to explain the payoff

words.prose: {{ar:أَمْرِهِمْ}} ({{tr:amrihim}}) names the deed as their own affair. The possessive suffix assigns responsibility to the brothers and aligns with the later independent {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}): the owners of the affair become the unaware subjects. The singular abstract noun gathers the whole plot into one case for future disclosure, especially once {{ar:هَذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) specifies it, while the root command and authority range sets their matter against God accomplishing His amr (65:3).

topics.headline: owned affair under divine contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hidden act is possessed by the brothers as one specific case, while God's amr remains the larger contrast.
topics.reason: The possessed singular noun is the topic of the informing promise; command/authority branches are narrowed to contrastive pressure.

words.gloss_range: proximal masculine singular demonstrative specifying this affair

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:هَذَا}} ({{tr:hādhā}}) points to the brothers affair as this particular deed. Its masculine singular form agrees with {{ar:أَمْر}} ({{tr:amr}}), not with the plural brothers, so the object of disclosure is one defined matter and not the group in general. The near demonstrative also makes the hidden deed present in divine speech, sealing the disclosure target before the ayah turns to their non-perception.

topics.headline: this exact affair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promised disclosure is restricted to this exact, near, singular affair rather than a vague account of the brothers.
topics.reason: QAC marks a masculine singular demonstrative used with the affair noun, supporting specificity and near deixis.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial conjunction introducing the brothers non-perception state
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the closing clause as both addition and circumstance: the brothers are in a state of not perceiving while the promised reversal is secured. The particle lets the closure say and and while at once, so their ignorance is not a loose afterthought but the condition around the promise. Its position after the emphatic disclosure makes the irony simultaneous and final, and the compact closing cadence turns concealment back on the plotters.

topics.headline: circumstantial ironic closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers ignorance is both the accompanying condition and final irony of the promised reversal.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the final nominal clause as circumstantial inside the revealed content.

words.gloss_range: independent 3MP pronoun foregrounding the brothers in the closing state

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) makes the brothers explicit even though the final verb could carry a plural subject by itself. The independent pronoun places them visibly inside the state of non-perception and gives the clause a nominal, stative feel rather than a one-time past mistake. It also links the owners of {{ar:أَمْرِهِمْ}} ({{tr:amrihim}}) to the subjects of ignorance, with the nasal texture of hum binding them audibly to the final perception verb.

topics.headline: explicit unaware subjects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the brothers made explicit as the owners of the affair and as subjects inhabiting non-perception.
topics.reason: QAC marks an independent 3MP pronoun as subject of the circumstantial clause.

words.gloss_range: negative particle scoping over the imperfect perception verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby word or phrase cited to explain the local payoff

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) negates the imperfect verb, keeping the brothers non-perception current rather than confined to a completed past failure. The construction is not a past-tense {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) negation; it presents their blindness as active during the promise and lets the ayah land on absence of perception rather than on their action. It also places the phrase within a recurring Quranic pattern of unaware actors, with 6:123 offering a clear plotter-unawareness parallel.

topics.headline: ongoing non-perception negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the brothers blindness is ongoing and formulaic, not a completed past failure.
topics.reason: QAC marks a negative particle before an imperfect verb; rows contrast it with a past jussive construction and with formulaic non-perception.

words.gloss_range: imperfect plural perception verb closing the ayah under negation
words.root_gloss_range: sensing, awareness, fine perception, and subtle recognition; local negated imperfect selects ongoing lack of perception
words.prose: {{ar:يَشْعُرُونَ}} ({{tr:yashʿurūn}}) closes the ayah on the brothers lack of perception. The verb has no explicit object, so the blindness is broad: they do not sense the revelation, the future disclosure, or the reversal already underway. The root fine-perception range sharpens the irony, the imperfect plural and final -un sound carry their collective unawareness into the ayah ending, and the same formulaic field appears with plotters unaware of self-harm in 6:123, heedless speakers in 49:2, and non-perception of resurrection timing in 27:65.

topics.headline: objectless final perception failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices broad, objectless non-perception closing the ayah as an ongoing collective failure of subtle awareness.
topics.reason: The verb lacks an explicit object and is negated in final position; fine-sense and formulaic rows are retained as narrowed pressure around the local perception verb.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The hidden depth of the well, the covert revelation to him, and their lack of perception.
baseline_models.mechanism: The brothers use a low cavity to remove Joseph from sight, but at that same point a second hidden channel delivers knowledge into the cavity. Spatial concealment and epistemic disclosure coincide, leaving the concealers outside the knowledge held by the concealed.

activation_trace.role: A low place in which something disappears supplies the spatial enclosure used to hide Joseph.
A cut, unlined well supplies the material container that removes him from ordinary sight.
Knowledge delivered covertly supplies a counter-channel inside the visual enclosure.
Fine apprehension supplies the epistemic capacity explicitly absent from the brothers.

changed_reading.before: They hide Joseph in a well and he receives private consolation.
changed_reading.after: Their concealment becomes the site of asymmetric knowledge: his body is hidden from eyes while future truth is deposited in him beyond their perception.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: They resolved to place him, yet he is promised that he will report this very affair of theirs.
baseline_models.mechanism: Collective resolve turns Joseph into the object of a managed placement, but the promise converts the same affair from an operation they control into the content of his future report. Agency reverses without the placement itself being undone.

activation_trace.role: Opinion gathered into firm resolve supplies closure and intentional unity to the plot.
Causing something to occupy a state supplies their attempt to determine Joseph's position and status.
A report that arrives and is delivered supplies Joseph's future counter-agency.
The affair as an identifiable state of things supplies the stable object that can later be reported back to its authors.

changed_reading.before: The verse promises that Joseph will one day tell them what happened.
changed_reading.after: The operation they author is already being converted into evidence that its object will later authoritatively report.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: They carry him away, place him in the well, and the sentence still projects him as a future speaker.
baseline_models.mechanism: Movement, a root-cutting image in the well root, and a receiving cavity compose a controlled severance from his present social location. The emphatic future report prevents that severance from functioning as narrative termination.

activation_trace.role: Going and passing away supplies the outward transport that begins the severance.
Cutting from the origin supplies the social-severance image latent in the chosen destination.
A cavity into which something enters supplies containment rather than annihilation.
The promised delivered report keeps the deposited person active beyond the attempted cut.

changed_reading.before: They take him away and put him into a pit.
changed_reading.after: They enact a social cutting and containment, but the sentence makes the contained person, not the cutting, the continuing agent.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: You will surely report it to them while they do not perceive.
baseline_models.mechanism: The emphatic future report followed by the circumstantial clause keeps two temporal attachments live. They may fail to perceive the revelation and its consequence now, or fail to perceive Joseph's identity or the significance of his report when the promise is fulfilled.

activation_trace.role: Covertly delivered knowledge supports present unawareness at the moment of revelation.
A future delivered report opens a later scene to which the unawareness clause may attach.
Fine recognition, when negated, can mark either current non-perception or later non-recognition.

changed_reading.before: The brothers simply do not notice the revelation in the well.
changed_reading.after: The clause can preserve both present ignorance and a future encounter in which they hear without recognizing, so the verse folds two epistemic scenes together.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening frame calls the discourse visible signs and a manifest book, then presents revelation as sequential recounting. Against that frame, the hidden affair in 12:15 is already undergoing the disclosure promised within it: what the actors conceal becomes a sign and narrated trace for an audience outside their awareness.

activation_trace.role: A visible sign supplies the public legibility into which the hidden incident is transformed.
Emergence and uncovering supply the disclosure pole opposed to the pit's concealment.
A report carried in sequence supplies the narrative process that makes the concealed affair public.
Being screened from eyes supplies the hidden event that the framing discourse is already revealing.

structural_cues: 12:1 frames what follows as signs of a manifest book.
12:3 frames the discourse as revelation and ordered recounting, while 12:15 contains revelation about a future report.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies manifest-sign framing, sequential recounting, and a hidden affair promised as report; I infer a bridge between the story level and the present act of narration. The live alternative is that the opening frame remains general rather than locally transforming 12:15.

changed_reading.before: The revelation is private reassurance delivered inside the pit.
changed_reading.after: The sentence also performs its own promise: the hidden act is already being carried into a manifest sign and narrated trace beyond the brothers' awareness.

context_deltas.mechanism: Joseph was told not to recount his vision because recounting would activate the brothers' scheme. The focus promise reverses that relation: the scheme activated by a threatened narrative becomes the very narrative he will deliver to them.

activation_trace.role: Sequentially conveying a report supplies the earlier act of telling that had to be withheld.
Cunningly managed deception supplies the threatened response to Joseph's first possible telling.
The promised delivered report turns the resulting scheme into a second, unavoidable telling.
Their affair supplies the new content generated by the attempt to suppress the earlier report.

structural_cues: 12:5 orders Joseph not to recount the vision and gives the brothers' scheme as the reason.
12:15 promises Joseph an emphatic future report addressed to those same brothers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an earlier prohibited telling, the scheme it might provoke, and the later promise of telling the schemers; I infer a silence-to-testimony reversal. The live alternative is that the promise offers comfort without deliberately answering the earlier prohibition.

changed_reading.before: Their plot will eventually be disclosed.
changed_reading.after: Their attempt to prevent one narrative from being told generates a second narrative whose content is their own attempt at suppression.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context first offers killing or expulsion, then explicitly rejects killing and substitutes casting into the well. Thus the focus's collective resolve is not original unanimity but convergence around a device that can satisfy removal while stopping short of direct killing.

activation_trace.role: Taking life supplies the lethal pole of the brothers' initial alternatives.
The explicit rejection of taking life supplies the constraint that reshapes the plan.
Casting something until it lies deposited supplies the substituted operation.
Firm resolve gathered from dispersed opinion supplies closure after the alternatives diverge.

structural_cues: 12:9 proposes either killing Joseph or casting him into another land.
12:10 rejects killing and proposes the hidden depth of the well; 12:15 records collective enactment of that placement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies competing proposals, an explicit correction, and final collective resolve; I infer that the well functions as compromise technology. A live alternative is simple dominance by one speaker rather than negotiated convergence.

changed_reading.before: All the brothers unanimously decide to put Joseph in the well.
changed_reading.after: Their unanimity is produced after disagreement, with the well materializing a compromise between lethal removal and continued life.

context_deltas.mechanism: The proposal pairs casting with pickup by a traveling group. The focus's hidden cavity therefore has two functions at once: it conceals Joseph from his kin network and exposes him to an unknown circulation network, turning enclosure into a handoff interface.

activation_trace.role: The deliberate casting supplies Joseph's deposition at the transfer point.
Taking up something found cast down supplies the receiving action anticipated beyond the brothers.
A moving group supplies the external transit network to which the well can hand him.
The low hidden place supplies concealment and temporary staging between two social fields.
The cut well supplies the material node where deposition can become pickup.

structural_cues: 12:10 grammatically links casting into the well to possible pickup by some travelers.
12:15 enacts the proposed placement but leaves the pickup outside its immediate frame.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies deposition, anticipated pickup, and a traveling group; I infer a spatial arrow from enclosure to transfer. The live alternative is that pickup is only one brother's hope and not part of the group's shared purpose.

changed_reading.before: The well is a sealed place of abandonment.
changed_reading.after: The well is also a transfer interface: concealment from one group creates exposure to another group's movement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The brothers twice define themselves as a mutually surrounding, supporting band. In the focus, their gathered resolve coheres around cutting one member from the family field; exclusion becomes the act through which the band performs its own unity.

activation_trace.role: A group that surrounds and supports one another supplies the brothers' self-image of collective cohesion.
The repeated surrounding group image reinforces cohesion immediately before the focus action.
Joining with others in complicity supplies the shared act that performs the band's unity.
Cutting from the origin supplies the exclusion around which that shared unity is organized.

structural_cues: 12:8 and 12:14 repeat the brothers' claim that they are an عصبة.
12:15 compresses their joint resolve, Joseph's changed placement, and the well into one coordinated action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a self-described cohesive band and a root-cutting branch at the band's shared destination; I infer social bonding through exclusion. The live alternative is that عصبة denotes strength only and carries no group-formation mechanism here.

changed_reading.before: The group coordinates to exclude Joseph.
changed_reading.after: The group's exclusion of Joseph also becomes a way of manufacturing and displaying its own internal cohesion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The brothers obtain access by asking to be trusted, claiming unmixed goodwill, requesting that Joseph be sent, and promising guard. The focus's taking-away is therefore not raw seizure but a custody transfer whose protective vocabulary is inverted into the means of concealment.

activation_trace.role: Security and settled trust supply the permission structure the brothers solicit.
Purity from deceit supplies the claimed quality that masks their actual intent.
Sending someone forth supplies the father's requested transfer of access.
Watchful guarding supplies the custody obligation they explicitly claim.
Taking advantage of another's heedlessness supplies the vulnerability named in the father's forecast.
Their going away with Joseph supplies the physical action enabled by the entrusted access.

structural_cues: 12:11-12 moves from a request for trust and a claim of sincerity to sending and promised guarding.
12:13 names feared harm during heedlessness; 12:15 begins only after the brothers have successfully gone away with Joseph.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies solicited trust, claimed sincerity, sending, guarding, and subsequent removal; I infer that protective speech functions as the access mechanism for the act. The live alternative is ordinary persuasion rather than a deliberately inverted custody structure.

changed_reading.before: The brothers physically take Joseph away and hide him.
changed_reading.after: They convert entrusted guardianship into access, so the concealment is also a breach produced through the language of protection.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same going-root links the father's warning, the actual taking-away, and the brothers' later account of going to race. Their real movement with Joseph is overwritten by a claimed movement away from Joseph, while leaving him behind supplies the invented gap in custody.

activation_trace.role: Going away supplies the father's anticipated movement with Joseph.
Going away supplies the actual transport that executes the plot.
Going away reappears as the opening motion of the brothers' replacement account.
Racing ahead supplies the distracting purpose assigned to their claimed movement.
Leaving something behind supplies the fabricated custody gap in which the reported harm could occur.

structural_cues: 12:13 predicts the brothers' going away with Joseph; 12:15 narrates that movement as fact.
12:17 repeats going but gives racing and leaving Joseph as its new causal sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a threefold lexical echo and two incompatible movement scenarios; I infer that the later motion rewrites the real one as alibi. The live alternative is ordinary repetition without deliberate lexical camouflage.

changed_reading.before: Going away is merely the first physical step of the plot.
changed_reading.after: Going away becomes the contested narrative hinge: warning, deed, and alibi reuse one motion while reversing who was taken and who was left.

context_deltas.mechanism: After the hidden act, the brothers arrive in low visibility with performed crying and a shirt made to carry false blood; the context finally names what they describe. These audible and visible surfaces try to govern perception, while the covert revelation in 12:15 creates a hidden witness who will report the affair they stage but do not perceive.

activation_trace.role: Covertly delivered knowledge supplies the counterwitness hidden beneath the manufactured surfaces.
Fine apprehension, denied to the brothers, supplies the epistemic failure beneath their evidence-making.
Night darkness and reduced clarity supply a low-visibility setting for presenting the alibi.
Affected crying supplies the audible surface meant to certify the account.
The worn shirt supplies the portable visual exhibit on which the false account is staged.
A garment that lies by its condition supplies the material-deception mechanism of the exhibit.
Making a thing appear through its attributed features supplies the brothers' descriptive control of the event.

structural_cues: 12:16 places the brothers' weeping arrival at night.
12:18 combines Joseph's shirt, false blood, Jacob's rejection, and an appeal for help against what they describe.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies low visibility, crying, a blood-marked shirt, falsehood, and description; I infer coordinated sensory evidence-making opposed by hidden testimony. The live alternative is a simple spoken lie with props rather than a systematic contest over perception.

changed_reading.before: The brothers fail to perceive the private revelation given to Joseph.
changed_reading.after: Their non-perception is ironic: they manufacture what others should hear and see while failing to perceive the hidden witness who will eventually describe their own affair.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus calls the deed this affair of theirs; Jacob then says their own selves have made an affair attractive. The repeated affair-root lets immediate diagnosis and promised future testimony converge on a stable object: an internally fashioned operation that can be named despite its false description.

activation_trace.role: An identifiable affair supplies the object Joseph is promised he will report.
The self's beautification of an act supplies the internal manufacture behind the external story.
What lies in the self as thought and inward prompting supplies the workshop in which the affair is made acceptable.
The repeated identifiable affair supplies Jacob's immediate external diagnosis of the same operation.
The future delivered report supplies the later direct naming that will answer the self-fashioned account.

structural_cues: 12:15 uses a deictic expression for their affair and promises that Joseph will report it.
12:18 rejects the brothers' account by diagnosing an affair their selves have made attractive.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated affair language, inward beautification, immediate diagnosis, and future report; I infer that both verses point to one stabilized case beneath the alibi. The live alternative is ordinary lexical repetition without a forensic naming function.

changed_reading.before: Their affair is a generic label for what they did.
changed_reading.after: Their affair is a self-fashioned but already diagnosable case that persists beneath their description and awaits direct testimony from Joseph.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The buried-tree-root image is cross-domain and should be rendered only as a material analogy, not as the lexical sense of غيابة here. It remains anchored in the focus root and is worth carrying because hidden roots that later appear sharply model the verse's move from underground concealment to promised future report.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Joseph is placed in the غيابة, yet is promised that he will later report the act.

activation_trace.role: Tree roots hidden underground and later exposed supply an emergence analogy for latent testimony.
Cutting from the origin supplies the attempted severance against which buried continuance persists.
The future delivered report supplies the eventual surfacing of what the pit holds latent.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the pit resembles earth holding a hidden root: attempted severance becomes a latent form of later emergence and testimony.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: Treating the garment as performing deception is a branch-driven material reading, not a claim that the syntax literally makes the shirt a speaking liar. It remains validly anchored in the shirt and falsehood roots and preserves the sharp contrast between a material exhibit that lies by appearance and the hidden person promised future speech.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The hidden Joseph is promised speech about the affair that the later shirt is made to misdescribe.

activation_trace.role: The shirt as a worn object supplies the material carrier of the brothers' account.
A garment that lies through its condition supplies deception enacted by an arranged object.
Joseph's future delivered report supplies the personal counter-speech to the garment's staged account.

changed_reading.before: The brothers lie verbally and use the shirt as supporting evidence.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the shirt itself performs their lie by its arranged condition, while the person displaced from view remains the future speaking counter-evidence.

strongest_changes: The pit is simultaneously a device of visual concealment and the site where hidden counterknowledge is installed.
Context recasts the well as both a compromise after competing proposals and a transfer interface to a traveling network.
The repeated going-root turns physical movement into a contested sequence of warning, deed, and alibi.
The aftermath stages visible and audible evidence against a covert witness, making perception itself the field of conflict.
summary.what_was_special: The focus compresses bodily placement, social severance, covert disclosure, future testimony, and failed perception into one hinge. Context activates several coexisting readings without resolving the temporal ambiguity of وهم لا يشعرون: the concealed victim becomes knower, the group's compromise becomes a route, suppressed telling generates testimony, and fabricated surfaces are opposed by hidden speech.
remaining_uncertainties: The unawareness clause may attach primarily to the revelation scene, the future reporting scene, or deliberately remain available to both.
The well may represent a negotiated compromise, or merely the successful proposal of one brother.
Pickup by travelers may be part of shared intent, one speaker's preserving hope, or only an anticipated possibility.
The root-cutting, buried-root, and lying-garment readings are productive branch analogies but remain deliberately exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **One concentrated resolve is answered by hidden counter-information.** ج م ع B003 (concerted resolve), غ ي ب B001/B002 (hiddenness/low hiding place), and و ح ي B001 (hidden imparting) create a reversal: the brothers gather intention to hide Yusuf, while hidden communication preserves his future knowledge. I infer that concealment becomes the medium of a counter-plan. The pit reads as an epistemic chamber, not only a place of disposal.
2. **Subtle awareness is asymmetrically distributed.** ش ع ر B005 (subtle knowing) is negated of the brothers, while ن ب ء B002 (news brought and reported) is promised to Yusuf. I infer that their ignorance includes failure to perceive their future position as recipients of his report. The act already contains its later disclosure.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:89-90 fulfilled the concealed promise: Yusuf reported their act back to them when they did not yet recognize him, then recognition broke open.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Report as reversal of narrative control.** `ن ب ء:B002` is consequential “news brought and reported,” while `ن ب ء:B001` retains movement or arrival from one place to another. The brothers make Joseph disappear, then arrive with their own report (12:16-18); the caravan’s arrival and his sale follow (12:19-20). Those movements and reports are supplied; I infer that survival will let the concealed object of their account become its informed narrator. *Latunabbiʾannahum* reads as a promised transfer of report-authority from plotters to the one plotted against.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:102 reports the very concealed gathering in which this future notification was announced, completing the reversal: those who controlled the secret become objects of a report beyond their control.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyi fark edip bilme, ona dikkatle uyanma, bilmeyi dileme, bilgiyi sağlayan şeyi sorma ve duyular yoluyla algılama kullanımlarını birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve ince farkındalık ve algı ortaklığını doğru biçimde yakalar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Karışık ve yalın olmayan kapsam, fark edip bilme çekirdeğini bilme dileği, bilgi sorusu ve duyulara özgü kalıplardan ayırmayı gerektirir; kalıp anlamları bütün dala yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi ince bir dikkatle fark etmek, algılamak ve böylece bilmek dalın çekirdeğidir. Bilmeyi dile getiren kalıp, neyin bilgi vereceğini soran anlatım ve algıyı sağlayan duyular bu çekirdeğe bağlı kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyi dikkatle fark edip algılayarak bilmek temel anlamı oluşturur.
Bir durumu bilmeyi dileme ve neyin onu bildireceğini sorma kalıpları, bilme çekirdeğinin söylem içindeki kullanımlarıdır.
Görme, işitme ve benzeri duyular, dünyayı algılayıp bilmeye yarayan yetiler olarak bu alana bağlanır.
